/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_complete_work
 *
 * Description:
 *   Work-queue half of buffer completion.  Drains doneq and reports each
 *   buffer to the upper half.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void bk7258_audio_complete_work(FAR void *arg)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = arg;
  FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
  irqstate_t flags;

  for (; ; )
    {
      flags = enter_critical_section();
      apb = (FAR struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_remfirst(&priv->doneq);
      leave_critical_section(flags);

      if (apb == NULL)
        {
          break;
        }

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
      priv->dev.upper(priv->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE, apb, OK,
                      NULL);
#else
      priv->dev.upper(priv->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE, apb, OK);
#endif
    }
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_finish
 *
 * Description:
 *   Move a finished buffer to doneq and schedule the completion work.
 *   Called from interrupt context.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void bk7258_audio_finish(FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv,
                                FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb)
{
  dq_addlast(&apb->dq_entry, &priv->doneq);

  if (work_available(&priv->work))
    {
      work_queue(HPWORK, &priv->work, bk7258_audio_complete_work, priv, 0);
    }
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_tx_callback
 *
 * Description:
 *   DAC FIFO service, invoked from the AUD ISR when the left FIFO has
 *   drained below its read threshold.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void bk7258_audio_tx_callback(void *arg)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = arg;
  FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
  unsigned int budget = BK7258_AUDIO_ISR_BUDGET;

  while (budget > 0)
    {
      apb = (FAR struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_peek(&priv->pendq);
      if (apb == NULL)
        {
          /* Nothing left to play.  Mask the interrupt so the ISR does not
           * spin on a permanently-empty FIFO; enqueuebuffer() re-arms it.
           */

          bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(false);
          return;
        }

      if (apb->curbyte + sizeof(int16_t) <= apb->nbytes)
        {
          FAR const int16_t *samples =
            (FAR const int16_t *)(apb->samp + apb->curbyte);
          unsigned int avail = (apb->nbytes - apb->curbyte) /
                               sizeof(int16_t);
          unsigned int written;

          if (avail > budget)
            {
              avail = budget;
            }

          written = bk7258_aud_dac_write(samples, avail);
          apb->curbyte += written * sizeof(int16_t);
          budget -= written;

          if (written < avail)
            {
              /* FIFO is full: come back on the next interrupt. */

              return;
            }
        }
      else
        {
          /* Buffer exhausted (this also covers a zero-length buffer, which
           * the upper half uses to mark end of stream).
           */

          (void)dq_remfirst(&priv->pendq);
          bk7258_audio_finish(priv, apb);
        }
    }
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_rx_callback
 *
 * Description:
 *   ADC FIFO service, invoked from the AUD ISR when the FIFO has risen
 *   above its write threshold.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_CAPTURE
static void bk7258_audio_rx_callback(void *arg)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = arg;
  FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
  unsigned int budget = BK7258_AUDIO_ISR_BUDGET;

  while (budget > 0)
    {
      apb = (FAR struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_peek(&priv->pendq);
      if (apb == NULL)
        {
          /* No buffer to fill.  Drop the interrupt rather than spinning;
           * the samples still in the FIFO are lost, which is the correct
           * behaviour for a capture overrun.
           */

          bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(false);
          return;
        }

      if (apb->nbytes + sizeof(int16_t) <= apb->nmaxbytes)
        {
          FAR int16_t *samples = (FAR int16_t *)(apb->samp + apb->nbytes);
          unsigned int room = (apb->nmaxbytes - apb->nbytes) /
                              sizeof(int16_t);
          unsigned int read;

          if (room > budget)
            {
              room = budget;
            }

          read = bk7258_aud_adc_read(samples, room);
          apb->nbytes += read * sizeof(int16_t);
          budget -= read;

          if (read < room)
            {
              /* FIFO drained: wait for the next interrupt. */

              return;
            }
        }
      else
        {
          (void)dq_remfirst(&priv->pendq);
          bk7258_audio_finish(priv, apb);
        }
    }
}
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_flush
 *
 * Description:
 *   Return every queued buffer to the upper half.  Used by shutdown and
 *   stop so no buffer is stranded in the lower half.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static void bk7258_audio_flush(FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv)
{
  FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb;
  irqstate_t flags;

  for (; ; )
    {
      flags = enter_critical_section();
      apb = (FAR struct ap_buffer_s *)dq_remfirst(&priv->pendq);
      leave_critical_section(flags);

      if (apb == NULL)
        {
          break;
        }

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
      priv->dev.upper(priv->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE, apb, OK,
                      NULL);
#else
      priv->dev.upper(priv->dev.priv, AUDIO_CALLBACK_DEQUEUE, apb, OK);
#endif
    }

  bk7258_audio_complete_work(priv);
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_poll_adc
 *
 * Description:
 *   Diagnostic helper: drain the ADC FIFO by polling for roughly 200 ms,
 *   deliberately ignoring the interrupt path.  Returns the sample count and
 *   accumulates the sum of squares so the caller can report a mean square.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

static unsigned int bk7258_audio_poll_adc(FAR uint64_t *sumsq)
{
  int16_t samples[32];
  unsigned int total = 0;
  unsigned int i;

  for (i = 0; i < 200; i++)
    {
      unsigned int got = bk7258_aud_adc_read(samples, 32);
      unsigned int j;

      for (j = 0; j < got; j++)
        {
          *sumsq += (uint64_t)((int32_t)samples[j] * (int32_t)samples[j]);
        }

      total += got;
      up_udelay(1000);
    }

  return total;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_getcaps
 ****************************************************************************/

static int bk7258_audio_getcaps(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, int type,
                                FAR struct audio_caps_s *caps)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;

  (void)type;

  DEBUGASSERT(caps != NULL &&
              caps->ac_len >= sizeof(struct audio_caps_s));

  caps->ac_format.hw  = 0;
  caps->ac_controls.w = 0;

  switch (caps->ac_type)
    {
      case AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY:

        /* Playback is mono: the chip has no right DAC and the board has a
         * single speaker.  Capture reports two channels when the MIC2 echo
         * reference is enabled, because frames really are L/R interleaved
         * (L = voice, R = reference) even though only one of the two is a
         * microphone.
         */

        caps->ac_channels = priv->playback ? 1 :
                            (priv->cfg.capture_reference ? 2 : 1);

        switch (caps->ac_subtype)
          {
            case AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY:
              caps->ac_controls.b[0] = priv->playback ? AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT :
                                                        AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT;
              caps->ac_format.hw = 1 << (AUDIO_FMT_PCM - 1);
              break;

            default:
              caps->ac_controls.b[0] = AUDIO_SUBFMT_END;
              break;
          }
        break;

      case AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT:
      case AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT:
        caps->ac_channels = priv->playback ? 1 :
                            (priv->cfg.capture_reference ? 2 : 1);

        switch (caps->ac_subtype)
          {
            case AUDIO_TYPE_QUERY:

              /* Only the rates reachable from the 26 MHz crystal are
               * advertised.  The 44.1k/48k families additionally need the
               * APLL calibration sequence, which aud_clk_config() in
               * bk7258_aud.c deliberately rejects with -ENOTSUP until it
               * has been transcribed from the vendor tree.
               */

              caps->ac_controls.hw[0] = AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_8K |
                                        AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_16K |
                                        AUDIO_SAMP_RATE_32K;
              caps->ac_controls.b[2] = 16;   /* Bits per sample */
              break;

            default:
              break;
          }
        break;

      /* Read back what configure(AUDIO_FU_VOLUME) last set, in the same
       * 0..1000 units it takes.  Without this a user interface can only show
       * the value it sent itself, which is a different claim: it would still
       * read 50% after something else changed the gain, and after a reboot it
       * would show a remembered number rather than the 0 dB the device
       * actually came up at.
       */

#ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_VOLUME
      case AUDIO_TYPE_FEATURE:
        if (caps->ac_format.hw == AUDIO_FU_VOLUME && priv->playback)
          {
            /* Rounded for the same reason as the other direction, and to the
             * same half step, so set(x) followed by get() returns x for every
             * value that is a real gain step.
             */

            caps->ac_controls.hw[0] =
              (uint16_t)(((uint32_t)priv->cfg.dac_dig_gain * 1000u +
                          BK7258_AUD_DAC_DIG_GAIN_MAX / 2) /
                         BK7258_AUD_DAC_DIG_GAIN_MAX);
            caps->ac_channels = 1;
          }
        else
          {
            caps->ac_subtype = 0;
            caps->ac_channels = 0;
          }
        break;
#endif

      default:
        caps->ac_subtype = 0;
        caps->ac_channels = 0;
        break;
    }

  return caps->ac_len;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_configure
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
static int bk7258_audio_configure(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                                  FAR void *session,
                                  FAR const struct audio_caps_s *caps)
#else
static int bk7258_audio_configure(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                                  FAR const struct audio_caps_s *caps)
#endif
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;
  uint32_t samplerate;
  int ret;

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
  (void)session;
#endif

  DEBUGASSERT(caps != NULL);

  switch (caps->ac_type)
    {
      case AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT:
      case AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT:
        if ((caps->ac_type == AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT) != priv->playback)
          {
            return -EINVAL;
          }

        /* Sample width.  The FIFO ports are 16 bits per sample and the
         * copy loops below step by sizeof(int16_t), so anything else would
         * be silently misinterpreted rather than merely sounding wrong.
         */

        if (caps->ac_controls.b[2] != 0 && caps->ac_controls.b[2] != 16)
          {
            auderr("unsupported sample width %u\n",
                   caps->ac_controls.b[2]);
            return -EINVAL;
          }

        /* Channel count.  Playback is mono because the chip has no right
         * DAC.  Capture is two channels when the MIC2 echo reference is
         * enabled and one otherwise; the count is a property of the
         * hardware wiring, not something the caller can choose.
         */

        if (caps->ac_channels != 0)
          {
            uint8_t expected = priv->playback ? 1 :
                               (priv->cfg.capture_reference ? 2 : 1);

            if (caps->ac_channels != expected)
              {
                auderr("unsupported channel count %u, expected %u\n",
                       caps->ac_channels, expected);
                return -EINVAL;
              }
          }

        /* nxplayer splits the sample rate across hw[0] and b[3] (see
         * nxplayer.c:1935-1936), so both halves have to be recombined.
         */

        samplerate = caps->ac_controls.hw[0] |
                     ((uint32_t)caps->ac_controls.b[3] << 16);
        if (samplerate != 0)
          {
            priv->cfg.samplerate = samplerate;
          }

        if (priv->playback)
          {
            ret = bk7258_aud_dac_setup(&priv->cfg);
          }
        else
          {
            ret = bk7258_aud_adc_setup(&priv->cfg);
          }

        if (ret < 0)
          {
            auderr("%s setup failed: %d\n",
                   priv->playback ? "DAC" : "ADC", ret);
            return ret;
          }

        priv->configured = true;
        break;

      case AUDIO_TYPE_FEATURE:

        /* Volume maps onto the DAC's digital gain.  The upper half passes
         * 0..1000; scale that onto 0..0x3f, whose 0 dB point is 0x2d.
         */

#ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_VOLUME
        if (caps->ac_format.hw == AUDIO_FU_VOLUME && priv->playback)
          {
            uint16_t volume = caps->ac_controls.hw[0];
            uint8_t gain;

            if (volume > 1000)
              {
                volume = 1000;
              }

            /* Rounded, not truncated.  Truncating loses a step in both
             * directions and the two losses compound: 0 dB is gain 0x2d, which
             * reports as 714, and 714 truncated back is 0x2c -- so asking for
             * the value the device itself reported moved the gain down a step
             * and reported 698, which no amount of clicking could get back to
             * 714.  Half a step of rounding here makes the round trip stable,
             * which is what a slider needs to be usable at all.
             */

            gain = (uint8_t)((volume * BK7258_AUD_DAC_DIG_GAIN_MAX + 500) /
                             1000);

            /* Kept in cfg as well as written to the register, because
             * dac_setup() rewrites the same GAIN field from cfg on every
             * AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT configure (bk7258_aud.c, the modifyreg32 over
             * BK7258_AUD_DAC_GAIN_MASK).  Writing only the register made a
             * volume last until the next playback started and then silently
             * revert to 0 dB -- which is why audio_test has to send -v after
             * its PCM configure rather than before.  Volume is a property of
             * the device, so it has to survive being reconfigured.
             */

            priv->cfg.dac_dig_gain = gain;

            return bk7258_aud_dac_set_dig_gain(gain);
          }

#endif
        return -ENOTTY;

      default:
        return -ENOTTY;
    }

  return OK;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_shutdown
 ****************************************************************************/

static int bk7258_audio_shutdown(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;

  if (priv->playback)
    {
      /* Amplifier first, DAC second: see bk7258_audio_stop(). */

      bk7258_aud_dac_mute(true);
      bk7258_audio_pa_enable(false);
      bk7258_aud_dac_shutdown();
    }
  else
    {
      bk7258_aud_adc_shutdown();
    }

  bk7258_audio_flush(priv);

  priv->configured = false;
  priv->running = false;
  priv->paused = false;

  return OK;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_start
 *
 * Description:
 *   Playback start-up order follows the vendor's onboard_speaker_stream
 *   implementation (aud_dac start, pa_on_delay, amplifier on, un-mute):
 *   the amplifier stays muted while the DAC's analog output settles, so
 *   the speaker does not pop.  R71's 10K pull-down keeps CTRL low until
 *   bk7258_audio_pa_enable(true) drives it, which means the hardware is
 *   already silent before software gets here.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
static int bk7258_audio_start(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                              FAR void *session)
#else
static int bk7258_audio_start(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
#endif
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
  (void)session;
#endif

  if (!priv->configured)
    {
      return -EPERM;
    }

  if (priv->running)
    {
      return OK;
    }

  if (priv->playback)
    {
      bk7258_aud_set_tx_callback(bk7258_audio_tx_callback, priv);
      bk7258_aud_dac_start();

      nxsig_usleep(CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_PA_ON_DELAY_MS * 1000);

      bk7258_audio_pa_enable(true);
      bk7258_aud_dac_mute(false);

      bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(true);
    }
#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_CAPTURE
  else
    {
      bk7258_aud_set_rx_callback(bk7258_audio_rx_callback, priv);
      bk7258_aud_adc_start();
      bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(true);
    }
#endif

  priv->running = true;
  priv->paused = false;

  return OK;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_stop
 *
 * Description:
 *   Teardown order is the inverse and is deliberately mute-first.  Note
 *   the vendor's own header and code disagree about where pa_off_delay
 *   sits: onboard_speaker_stream.h:51 describes it as the delay *after*
 *   turning the amplifier off, while onboard_speaker_stream.c:341-345
 *   sleeps *before* pulling the GPIO low.  The code order is the one that
 *   actually lets the analog output settle while still muted, so that is
 *   what is implemented here.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_STOP
#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
static int bk7258_audio_stop(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                             FAR void *session)
#else
static int bk7258_audio_stop(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
#endif
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
  (void)session;
#endif

  if (priv->playback)
    {
      bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(false);

      bk7258_aud_dac_mute(true);
      nxsig_usleep(CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_PA_OFF_DELAY_MS * 1000);
      bk7258_audio_pa_enable(false);

      bk7258_aud_dac_stop();
    }
  else
    {
      bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(false);
      bk7258_aud_adc_stop();
    }

  if (priv->playback)
    {
      bk7258_aud_set_tx_callback(NULL, NULL);
    }
  else
    {
      bk7258_aud_set_rx_callback(NULL, NULL);
    }

  priv->running = false;
  priv->paused = false;

  bk7258_audio_flush(priv);

  return OK;
}
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_pause / bk7258_audio_resume
 *
 * Description:
 *   Pause only masks the FIFO interrupt and mutes; the DAC stays enabled
 *   and the amplifier stays on so resume is click-free.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifndef CONFIG_AUDIO_EXCLUDE_PAUSE_RESUME
#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
static int bk7258_audio_pause(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                              FAR void *session)
#else
static int bk7258_audio_pause(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
#endif
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
  (void)session;
#endif

  if (!priv->running || priv->paused)
    {
      return OK;
    }

  if (priv->playback)
    {
      bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(false);
      bk7258_aud_dac_mute(true);
    }
  else
    {
      bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(false);
    }

  priv->paused = true;
  return OK;
}

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
static int bk7258_audio_resume(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                               FAR void *session)
#else
static int bk7258_audio_resume(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
#endif
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
  (void)session;
#endif

  if (!priv->running || !priv->paused)
    {
      return OK;
    }

  if (priv->playback)
    {
      bk7258_aud_dac_mute(false);
      bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(true);
    }
  else
    {
      bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(true);
    }

  priv->paused = false;
  return OK;
}
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_enqueuebuffer
 ****************************************************************************/

static int bk7258_audio_enqueuebuffer(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                                      FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;
  irqstate_t flags;

  DEBUGASSERT(apb != NULL);

  if (priv->playback)
    {
      apb->curbyte = 0;
    }
  else
    {
      apb->nbytes = 0;
    }

  flags = enter_critical_section();
  dq_addlast(&apb->dq_entry, &priv->pendq);
  leave_critical_section(flags);

  /* The ISR masks its own interrupt when it runs out of buffers, so
   * re-arm here rather than relying on it staying enabled.
   */

  if (priv->running && !priv->paused)
    {
      if (priv->playback)
        {
          bk7258_aud_tx_int_enable(true);
        }
      else
        {
          bk7258_aud_rx_int_enable(true);
        }
    }

  return OK;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_cancelbuffer
 ****************************************************************************/

static int bk7258_audio_cancelbuffer(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                                     FAR struct ap_buffer_s *apb)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;
  irqstate_t flags;

  flags = enter_critical_section();
  dq_rem(&apb->dq_entry, &priv->pendq);
  leave_critical_section(flags);

  return OK;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_ioctl
 ****************************************************************************/

static int bk7258_audio_ioctl(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev, int cmd,
                              unsigned long arg)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *)dev;

  (void)priv;

  switch (cmd)
    {
      /* This must be answered unconditionally, and NOT hidden behind
       * CONFIG_AUDIO_DRIVER_SPECIFIC_BUFFERS.
       *
       * The upper half latches its buffer quota from this call:
       * audio.c:1267-1279 forwards GETBUFFERINFO to the lower half and only
       * assigns upper->nbuffers when the lower half returns >= 0.  If the
       * lower half answers -ENOTTY, upper->nbuffers stays 0, and then
       * audio_allocbuffer() (audio.c:786-789) short-circuits with
       * "return 0" on the very first AUDIOIOC_ALLOCBUFFER because
       * periods >= nbuffers already holds.  The application then cannot
       * obtain a single buffer, which is what "ALLOCBUFFER 0 failed: 0"
       * looked like on hardware.
       */

      case AUDIOIOC_GETBUFFERINFO:
        {
          FAR struct ap_buffer_info_s *bufinfo =
            (FAR struct ap_buffer_info_s *)arg;

          if (bufinfo == NULL)
            {
              return -EINVAL;
            }

          bufinfo->buffer_size = CONFIG_AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES;
          bufinfo->nbuffers    = CONFIG_AUDIO_NUM_BUFFERS;
        }
        break;

      /* Gain staging for the capture path.  Takes effect at the next
       * AUDIOIOC_CONFIGURE, which is where adc_setup() runs; applying it to a
       * stream already running would change the level mid-recording and make
       * the measurement it exists for meaningless.
       */

      case BK7258_AUDIOIOC_SET_CAPGAIN:
        {
          FAR const struct bk7258_audio_capgain_s *g =
            (FAR const struct bk7258_audio_capgain_s *)arg;

          if (g == NULL)
            {
              return -EINVAL;
            }

          if (priv->playback)
            {
              return -ENOTTY;
            }

          if (g->mic_gain > BK7258_AUD_MIC_GAIN_MAX ||
              g->adc_gain > BK7258_AUD_ADC_GAIN_MAX)
            {
              return -EINVAL;
            }

          priv->cfg.mic_gain = g->mic_gain;
          priv->cfg.adc_gain = g->adc_gain;
          priv->cfg.adc_hpf  = g->hpf;

          audinfo("capture gain: mic=%u adc=%u hpf=%d\n",
                  g->mic_gain, g->adc_gain, g->hpf);
        }
        break;

      /* Diagnostic: dump registers, then read the FIFO by polling so the
       * interrupt path is taken out of the picture entirely.
       */

      case BK7258_AUDIOIOC_DIAG:
        {
          unsigned int total = 0;
          uint64_t sumsq = 0;
          unsigned int i;

          syslog(LOG_INFO, "diag: %s, configured=%d running=%d "
                 "paused=%d rate=%" PRIu32 " ref=%d\n",
                 priv->playback ? "playback" : "capture",
                 priv->configured, priv->running, priv->paused,
                 priv->cfg.samplerate, priv->cfg.capture_reference);

          bk7258_aud_dump();

          if (!priv->playback)
            {
              bool forced;

              forced = bk7258_aud_force_module_clock();
              syslog(LOG_INFO, "diag: aud_cken was %s\n",
                     forced ? "CLEAR -> now set by AP" : "already set");

              /* Which MIC front end actually reaches the ADC?
               *
               * The ADC has been measured to deliver a single channel, so
               * the right half of every FIFO word is always zero and MIC2
               * never shows up in a normal capture.  Looking at MIC2 on
               * its own is the only way to tell whether the board's
               * post-amplifier echo tap (HT6872 OUT+/OUT- -> R84/R83 ->
               * C61/C60 -> MIC2P/MIC2N) carries signal at all, which is a
               * board-level question rather than a driver one.
               */

              bk7258_aud_select_mic(true, false);
              up_udelay(5000);
              sumsq = 0;
              total = bk7258_audio_poll_adc(&sumsq);
              syslog(LOG_INFO,
                     "diag: MIC1 only -> %u samples, meansq=%llu\n", total,
                     total ? (unsigned long long)(sumsq / total) : 0ull);

              bk7258_aud_select_mic(false, true);
              up_udelay(5000);
              sumsq = 0;
              total = bk7258_audio_poll_adc(&sumsq);
              syslog(LOG_INFO,
                     "diag: MIC2 only -> %u samples, meansq=%llu\n", total,
                     total ? (unsigned long long)(sumsq / total) : 0ull);

              /* Leave MIC1 selected again. */

              bk7258_aud_select_mic(true, priv->cfg.capture_reference);

              /* AUD_CLK_CONTROL sweep.
               *
               * Only bit0 (ADC_SOFT_RESET) and bit1 (ADC_CLK_GATE) exist,
               * so all four combinations can simply be tried in order,
               * polling after each.  This settles by experiment what the
               * vendor sources describe inconsistently: whether bit0 is a
               * pulse that must be cleared (this driver's current
               * behaviour) or a release that must stay asserted (what
               * bk_aud_driver_init() actually leaves behind).
               */

              for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)
                {
                  bk7258_aud_set_clk_control(i);
                  up_udelay(2000);

                  sumsq = 0;
                  total = bk7258_audio_poll_adc(&sumsq);

                  syslog(LOG_INFO,
                         "diag: clkctl=0x%x (rst=%d gate=%d) -> %u samples,"
                         " meansq=%llu fifosta=0x%08" PRIx32 "\n",
                         i, i & 1, (i >> 1) & 1, total,
                         total ? (unsigned long long)(sumsq / total) : 0ull,
                         bk7258_aud_fifo_status());
                }
            }

          syslog(LOG_INFO, "diag: fifo status after poll=0x%08" PRIx32 "\n",
                 bk7258_aud_fifo_status());
        }
        break;

      default:
        (void)arg;
        return -ENOTTY;
    }

  return OK;
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_reserve / bk7258_audio_release
 ****************************************************************************/

#ifdef CONFIG_AUDIO_MULTI_SESSION
static int bk7258_audio_reserve(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                                FAR void **session)
{
  (void)dev;

  if (session != NULL)
    {
      *session = NULL;
    }

  return OK;
}

static int bk7258_audio_release(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev,
                                FAR void *session)
{
  (void)dev;
  (void)session;
  return OK;
}
#else
static int bk7258_audio_reserve(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
{
  (void)dev;
  return OK;
}

static int bk7258_audio_release(FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *dev)
{
  (void)dev;
  return OK;
}
#endif

/****************************************************************************
 * Public Functions
 ****************************************************************************/

/****************************************************************************
 * Name: bk7258_audio_dev_initialize
 *
 * Description:
 *   Create one audio lower-half instance.  playback selects the DAC path;
 *   otherwise the ADC path is used.
 *
 ****************************************************************************/

FAR struct audio_lowerhalf_s *bk7258_audio_dev_initialize(bool playback)
{
  FAR struct bk7258_audio_s *priv;

  if (playback)
    {
      priv = &g_bk7258_playback;
    }
  else
    {
#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_CAPTURE
      priv = &g_bk7258_capture;
#else
      return NULL;
#endif
    }

  memset(priv, 0, sizeof(*priv));

  priv->dev.ops = &g_bk7258_audio_ops;
  priv->playback = playback;

  dq_init(&priv->pendq);
  dq_init(&priv->doneq);

  priv->cfg.samplerate   = CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_SAMPLERATE;
  priv->cfg.clksrc       = BK7258_AUD_CLK_XTAL;
  priv->cfg.dac_dig_gain = BK7258_AUD_DAC_DIG_GAIN_0DB;
  priv->cfg.dac_ana_gain = BK7258_AUD_DAC_ANA_GAIN_DEF;
  priv->cfg.adc_gain     = BK7258_AUD_ADC_GAIN_0DB;
  priv->cfg.mic_gain     = BK7258_AUD_MIC_GAIN_DEF;

  /* Bypassed, matching the vendor and everything measured so far.  The
   * high-pass stages are almost certainly the better setting for voice, but
   * flipping the default before the difference has been measured would mean
   * every later comparison starts from an unverified baseline.
   */

  priv->cfg.adc_hpf      = false;

#if defined(CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_CAPTURE) && \
    defined(CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO_AEC_REFERENCE)
  priv->cfg.capture_reference = !playback;
#else
  priv->cfg.capture_reference = false;
#endif

  return &priv->dev;
}

#endif /* CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO */

input.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does a volume setting survive somebody else starting playback?

This is the bug the driver change fixes.  configure(AUDIO_FU_VOLUME) wrote the
register but not priv->cfg, and dac_setup() rewrites the same GAIN field from
cfg on every AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT configure -- so a volume set from the page
lasted until the next `audio_test play` and then silently went back to 0 dB.

Set a value that is nowhere near unity, run a playback through a completely
different application, then read back.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import ssl
import sys

import aiohttp

URL = "https://127.0.0.1:8443/ws"


async def call(ws, n, cmd, args=None, timeout=40):
    await ws.send_str(json.dumps({"op": "cmd", "id": n, "cmd": cmd,
                                  "args": args or {}, "timeout": timeout}))
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    deadline = loop.time() + timeout + 5
    while loop.time() < deadline:
        msg = await asyncio.wait_for(ws.receive(), timeout=timeout + 5)
        if msg.type is not aiohttp.WSMsgType.TEXT:
            continue
        obj = json.loads(msg.data)
        if obj.get("type") == "rsp" and obj.get("id") == n:
            return obj
    raise TimeoutError(cmd)


async def main():
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
    ctx.check_hostname = False
    ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE

    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
        async with s.ws_connect(URL, ssl=ctx, max_msg_size=8 << 20) as ws:
            n = 300

            target = 200          # 20%, far from the 714 default
            print("=== 1. 设 %d（20%%），不播报以免干扰 ===" % target)
            r = await call(ws, n := n + 1, "audio.volume",
                           {"volume": target, "announce": False})
            before = r["data"]["volume"]
            print("   板子报 %s" % before)

            print("=== 2. 用 audio_test play 走完整播放流程 ===")
            r = await call(ws, n := n + 1, "shell.exec",
                           {"cmdline": "audio_test play -t 1"})
            print("   accepted=%s" % (r.get("data") or {}).get("accepted"))
            await asyncio.sleep(6)

            print("=== 3. 播放之后再读音量 ===")
            r = await call(ws, n := n + 1, "audio.volume")
            after = r["data"]["volume"]
            print("   板子报 %s" % after)

            if after == before:
                print("\nPASS 音量穿过播放存活（%s -> %s）" % (before, after))
                rc = 0
            else:
                print("\nFAIL 播放把音量改掉了：%s -> %s（0 dB 是 714）"
                      % (before, after))
                rc = 1

            print("=== 4. 恢复 0 dB 并播报 ===")
            await call(ws, n := n + 1, "audio.volume", {"volume": 714})
    return rc


sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))


你现在可以打开 `https://127.0.0.1:8443/`，拖滑块点应用，板子会用新音量念"音量设置成功"。设 30% 和设 71% 听起来会有明显差别。

# 这轮修了三个真实缺陷

**一、音量被下一次播放静默重置。** `AUDIO_FU_VOLUME` 只写寄存器不更新 `priv->cfg`，而播放的 `dac_setup()` 会用 `cfg` 重写同一个增益字段。实测已确认修复（206 穿过播放不变）。

**二、0 dB 点点不回去。** 两个方向都向下取整，误差叠加：`unity` 报 714，设 714 却落到 698。改成四舍五入后精确回环。

**三、读回永远是 null**（这个是我自己写出来的 bug，靠真板子才暴露）。驱动 `getcaps` 在 switch **之前**就把 `ac_format.hw` 清零了，而我的 `case` 正是靠这个字段判断要读哪个 feature —— 所以永远不匹配。mock 上没有这个清零行为，所以 137 项测试全过、真板子却是 null。修法是在清零前把请求值存下来，并**加了一条断言要求 volume 必须是数字而不是 null** —— 这样以后 mock 测不到的东西至少有一条会盯着。

# 也修了一个环境坑（跟代码无关）

我之前连着四次烧录失败，根因是两个叠加的问题：

```
which -a stdbuf
  /home/mi/vela/prebuilts/build-tools/linux-x86_64/bin/stdbuf   ← PATH 第一，找不到自己的 libstdbuf.so
  /usr/bin/stdbuf                                                ← 好的
```

`/home/mi/vela`（另一个工作区）的 prebuilts 被塞在 PATH 最前面，`autoflash.sh` 用 `stdbuf` 做行缓冲，于是在进握手循环前就退出。**以后烧录都要带 PATH 前缀**：

```bash
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin ./autoflash.sh
```

第二个是我自己造的：`pkill -f "cat /dev/ttyUSB0"` 杀不掉 `sg dialout -c "cat ..."` 起的进程，串口一直被占，第一次烧录中断把固件写坏，之后板子不响应软复位 —— 才需要你手按 RST。刚才这次板子固件是好的，软复位一次就成功了。

Looking at the screenshot, the layout works but there's significant wasted space in the taller cards like the preview and chat history sections, while the bottom panes take up too much room. The issue is that the grid rows are all equal height, so cards with minimal content end up with large empty areas below them.

I'm thinking the better approach is to make the cards size to their content and let the console and log panes expand to fill the remaining vertical space — they actually benefit from more room since they display output. So I'd restructure the grid rows to be auto-sized for the cards but let the bottom panes grow to fill whatever space is left.

The tricky part is preventing the cards from overflowing the viewport if their content gets too large, so I'd cap the cards section with a max-height and overflow, then let the dragger adjust that split dynamically. This way the layout stays dense at the top with no wasted space, and the user gets a bigger console area below.

Actually, I'm realizing my own volume read calculation might be off. Let me trace through: for gain 37, I get (37000+31)/63 = 587, which means the board's actual gain is 37, not 45. Something changed it between those two points — either the agent app's voice module is running and resetting volume, or audio_test play modified the DAC gain through a different code path.

37 in hex is 0x25, which isn't an obvious constant, so this is worth investigating since it suggests volume might not be stable in all cases. But I should finish the layout improvement first, then come back to verify the volume stability. I'm going to implement the cards with content-sized dimensions capped at a maximum, with the bottom section taking up the remaining space.

text:
找到了一个**真实缺陷**，而且是我引入的：

```
console: board link dropped: board stopped answering (no frame for 16s)
web_tool: announcement played, 16 buffer(s)
```

**播报是阻塞式的，会话线程在播的那 2 秒里不回 PING** —— 但 keepalive 只等 16 秒，而 layout_check 三次加载页面时每次都触发读音量/摄像头，叠加起来把会话线程占住太久，对端判定板子失联。

我在写 `wt_play_pcm` 时特意注释了"阻塞是故意的，只有 2 秒"，但漏了一点：**它阻塞的是要回 PING 的那条线程**。这是设计缺陷，不是偶发。

修法：播报期间先把 PONG 的责任让出去 —— 最简单可靠的做法是把播放放到独立线程，命令立即返回：

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The keepalive regression: does using the volume control kill the link?

Before the announcement was moved off the session thread, each apply blocked
that thread for the two seconds the clip lasted -- and that thread is the one
that answers PING.  A few applies in a row and the host declared the board dead
("board stopped answering (no frame for 16s)") while the board was healthy and
audibly playing.

So this hammers the control the way a person dragging a slider would, and then
asks the backend whether the link is still the same one.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import ssl
import sys

import aiohttp

URL = "https://127.0.0.1:8443/ws"


async def call(ws, n, cmd, args=None, timeout=30):
    await ws.send_str(json.dumps({"op": "cmd", "id": n, "cmd": cmd,
                                  "args": args or {}, "timeout": timeout}))
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    deadline = loop.time() + timeout + 5
    while loop.time() < deadline:
        msg = await asyncio.wait_for(ws.receive(), timeout=timeout + 5)
        if msg.type is not aiohttp.WSMsgType.TEXT:
            continue
        obj = json.loads(msg.data)
        if obj.get("type") == "rsp" and obj.get("id") == n:
            return obj
    raise TimeoutError(cmd)


async def state(ws, n):
    await ws.send_str(json.dumps({"op": "state", "id": n}))
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    deadline = loop.time() + 15
    while loop.time() < deadline:
        msg = await asyncio.wait_for(ws.receive(), timeout=15)
        if msg.type is not aiohttp.WSMsgType.TEXT:
            continue
        obj = json.loads(msg.data)
        if obj.get("type") == "rsp" and obj.get("id") == n:
            return obj["data"]["link"]
    raise TimeoutError("state")


async def main():
    ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
    ctx.check_hostname = False
    ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE

    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
        async with s.ws_connect(URL, ssl=ctx, max_msg_size=8 << 20) as ws:
            n = 400

            link0 = await state(ws, n := n + 1)
            print("开始: connected=%s host=%s"
                  % (link0.get("connected"), link0.get("host")))
            if not link0.get("connected"):
                print("FAIL 板子一开始就没接入")
                return 1

            levels = [200, 400, 600, 714, 300, 500, 714, 250]
            print("=== 连续 %d 次调音量，每次间隔 0.4 秒 ===" % len(levels))
            announced = 0
            busy = 0
            for i, v in enumerate(levels):
                r = await call(ws, n := n + 1, "audio.volume", {"volume": v})
                if not r.get("ok"):
                    print("   %d) FAIL %s" % (i + 1, r))
                    return 1
                d = r["data"]
                if d.get("announced"):
                    announced += 1
                elif d.get("announce_errname") == "EBUSY":
                    busy += 1
                print("   %d) 要 %-4d 得 %-4d 播报=%s%s"
                      % (i + 1, v, d.get("volume"), d.get("announced"),
                         "" if d.get("announced")
                         else " (%s)" % d.get("announce_errname")))
                await asyncio.sleep(0.4)

            print("   播报 %d 次，因忙跳过 %d 次" % (announced, busy))

            # The point of the whole test: the link must be the same one.
            await asyncio.sleep(3)
            link1 = await state(ws, n := n + 1)
            print("结束: connected=%s host=%s"
                  % (link1.get("connected"), link1.get("host")))

            if not link1.get("connected"):
                print("\nFAIL 链路掉了（正是修复前的症状）")
                return 1
            if link1.get("host") != link0.get("host"):
                print("\nFAIL 链路重连过：%s -> %s"
                      % (link0.get("host"), link1.get("host")))
                return 1

            r = await call(ws, n := n + 1, "sys.status")
            print("命令仍可用: ok=%s uptime=%s"
                  % (r.get("ok"), (r.get("data") or {}).get("uptime")))

            print("\nPASS 连续调音量后链路未断、未重连")
    return 0


sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

---
feat(audio_test): encode Ogg Opus, and stream it in chunks while recording
Three things arrive together because each one is what makes the next possible:
an encoder, a way off the board, and a capture that does not have to finish
before either runs.
Ogg Opus, not raw Opus packets.  Opus packets carry no sample rate, channel
count or packet boundaries, so a bare concatenation is not decodable without
side information.  Every recognition service that takes Opus takes it in Ogg
(RFC 7845), which costs 28 bytes of page header plus two small headers.  The
granule positions are in 48 kHz units whatever the input rate, so a 20 ms
frame advances the granule by 960 even though only 320 samples went in at
16 kHz; getting that wrong yields a file that decodes and misreports its own
length.
Getting it off the board, in the order the board could support it:
  - base64 over the console, because there was no network and the AP console
    is a mailbox path rather than a byte stream.  The relay queue, not the
    line rate, is the limit: 16 lines between pauses lost 23 lines out of a
    16 KiB dump, so it pauses every line and a CRC32 is printed with the
    length.  `dump` repeats the last encode so a mangled transfer costs one
    command instead of another recording.
  - `send` over TCP once the network worked, same bytes without base64's
    third of overhead.
  - `pcm` for raw samples, because a 16 kbps encoder is built to discard
    noise-like content, so a noise spectrum measured after it describes the
    encoder as much as the microphone.

input.text:
fix(bk7258): make the DAC volume a property of the device, not of the moment

Three defects in the playback volume path, all found by driving it from a
slider rather than from a one-shot command line.

The volume did not survive being reconfigured.  configure(AUDIO_FU_VOLUME)
wrote the DAC's gain register and left priv->cfg alone, while
bk7258_aud_dac_setup() rewrites that same GAIN field from priv->cfg on every
AUDIO_TYPE_OUTPUT configure.  So a volume set from anywhere lasted until the
next playback started and then silently reverted to 0 dB.  That is also why
audio_test has to pass -v after its PCM configure rather than before: the
ordering was working around this.  Measured on hardware: set 206, run
`audio_test play`, read back 714 before the fix and 206 after it.

There was no way to read the volume back.  getcaps answered nothing for
AUDIO_TYPE_FEATURE, so a user interface could only ever show the value it had
sent itself -- a different claim from what the device is set to, and wrong
after a reboot or after something else changed the gain.  It now reports the
current gain in the same 0..1000 units configure takes.

Both conversions truncated, and the two losses compounded.  0 dB is gain
0x2d, which reports as 714; 714 truncated back is 0x2c, so asking for the
value the device itself had just reported moved the gain down a step and
answered 698.  No amount of clicking could return to 714.  Both directions
now round to the nearest step, which makes set-then-get stable for every
value that is a real gain step.

One thing to know when reading getcaps: ac_format.hw is both an input (which
feature unit is being asked about) and an output, and the function clears the
reply fields before the switch.  The volume case therefore has to read it
first.  Getting that wrong made this look like it worked -- the host-side mock
has no such clearing and answered correctly -- while the board reported null.

input.text:
feat(conv): keep conversation history on the SD card and make it searchable

What the product needs to answer is "what did we talk about on the 14th" and
"which conversation mentioned 爬山", from a device that is carried around.  So
the history is text, and it lives on the persistent card rather than in the
agent's RAM disk.

Three properties of the filesystem shape the design, and all three were
measured on the board rather than assumed:

  - CONFIG_FAT_LFN is off, so names are 8.3.  A timestamp does not fit in
    eight characters, which rules out naming each record after its date and
    letting readdir() answer date queries.
  - CONFIG_FS_FATTIME is off, so there are no modification times either --
    stat() and filter on mtime is out for the same reason.
  - time(NULL) returns seconds since boot, not a wall clock: the first session
    uploaded was numbered 249.  The board cannot timestamp anything on its own.

So the date is data, in an index file, and it comes from outside.  The index
is the only file a query reads: one sequential pass answers date-range, cue and
confidence filters without opening a record.  A keyword then opens only the
transcripts that survived that pass, which is the difference between reading a
few hundred bytes and reading every conversation on the card.  The keyword
searches the summary as well as the transcript, because a conversation can be
about 爬山 with the word appearing only in the summary.

No audio is kept.  A record is the transcript and the expression analysis; the
text is what a person searches and reads back, it is two orders of magnitude
smaller, and keeping recordings of other people's conversations on a device
that is carried around is a liability nobody asked for.  Live audio still goes
to the cloud for recognition -- see audio_test's chunked upload.

The analysis is stored as social-cue/v1 and carried through unflattened,
including unable_to_judge and the per-cue confidence.  Flattening it to one
emotion label would turn a hedged reading of a face into an assertion about a
person, which is the opposite of what this product promises.

The index line is written after the record files on purpose.  A record whose
files exist but whose index line does not is invisible and harmless; an index
line pointing at files that were never finished is a query that fails.  If
power is lost mid-write, the cheaper failure is the one that happens.

conv_ws.c, conv_net.c and conv_serve.c are the `conv serve` path: a minimal
WebSocket client that answered queries from a plaintext relay on the
development machine.  It is superseded by web_tool, which carries the same
queries over TLS with the console's certificate pinned, and it should not be
used for anything that touches a credential -- `conv llm` over that path sends
an API key in the clear.  It is kept for now only because the store's own
commands (seed, list, get, clear) share the file layout with it.

text: 第三个：web_tool 板侧新命令 + 语音资产 + 测试：

input.text:
feat(web_tool): serve the conversation history, and make the volume audible

Three commands, all reading or writing something the page could not reach
before: conv.query, conv.get and audio.volume, plus audio.announce which puts
the spoken confirmation on the card.

conv.query and conv.get are app/conv's store, reached over the link that is
already there.  Only the reading half: writing a record is the recogniser's
job, and clearing history is destructive enough to be worth typing out on a
console rather than exposing to a page a stray click can drive.  The store is
compiled in through REALPATH rather than a relative path, because both
directories arrive here as <linkfile> symlinks under packages/demos/ whose
names do not match their source directories -- "../conv" resolves to
packages/demos/conv, which does not exist.

matched and returned are reported separately.  limit truncates the list but
the count is of everything that matched, because "57 matches, 20 shown" and
"20 matches" are different answers to the operator's question, and asking
conv_store_query() to stop early would have replaced the count with the
visitor's return value.

audio.volume reads with no argument and sets with one, so the page does not
need two round trips to show the result of its own change.  The answer is a
read-back, never an echo: the driver quantises to six bits of gain, so 300
comes back as 302, and reporting the request would invent a precision that
does not exist.  It also reports where 0 dB sits (714 of 1000) -- 100% is the
DAC amplifying by 1.4x, not "normal", and the page has to be able to say so.

No AUDIOIOC_RESERVE around it, deliberately: audio.c forwards
AUDIOIOC_CONFIGURE straight to the lower half without checking whether the
device is reserved, so the volume can be changed while something is playing,
which is when an operator wants to change it.  Reserving would have failed
with EBUSY exactly then.

Setting a volume plays "音量设置成功" at the new gain.  That is the point of
the control: a number on a slider does not tell anyone whether the board is
loud enough in the room they are standing in.  One fixed phrase rather than one
per level -- the level is carried by how loud the phrase is, so eleven
recordings would say the same thing eleven times.

The clip is on the card, not in the firmware: this configuration is at 92% of
a 1088 KB flash and the clip is 32 KB.  It is raw mono s16le at 8 kHz, no
header and no decoder in the path, which also makes "is it the volume or is it
the clip" answerable by ear.  8 kHz rather than 16 because at 16 the two-second
phrase is 63.7 KB against a 65.5 KB frame limit -- a limit met exactly today is
a limit that breaks on the next edit.

It plays on its own thread.  Blocking the session thread was the first attempt
and it broke the link: that thread reads the socket and answers PING from the
same loop, so two seconds of playback is two seconds of not answering, and the
host declares the board dead after sixteen.  Observed as "board stopped
answering (no frame for 16s)" while the board was healthy and audibly playing.
So the handler starts a thread and answers immediately, and `announced` means
"playback started" -- the response cannot claim the sound came out.

audio.announce uploads the clip in chunks with an explicit offset, checked
against the file position rather than trusted: base64 makes each chunk a third
larger than the raw bytes, so 32 KB is several requests, and a lost or
reordered one would otherwise produce a file of the right length and the wrong
sound.  A missing clip never fails the volume command -- the volume did take,
and folding that into a failure would say the setting was lost when it was not.

host/make_announce.sh renders the clip.  This machine has no offline TTS at all
and installing one needs root, so it uses edge-tts, which is a pip --user
install and needs no API key.  It does need to reach Microsoft once, which is
why the output is committed rather than rendered at build time.

input.text:
refactor(web_tool): put the new panels in, and fit the whole console on one screen

Two cards -- playback volume and conversation history -- and a layout that no
longer needs scrolling to reach a control.

The panels first.  The volume slider sends nothing until 应用: firing an ioctl
per pixel would put hundreds of requests on the wire for one gesture, and the
board answers each one.  The scale marks where 0 dB is instead of leaving 100%
to read as "normal", and above it the page says the DAC is amplifying and can
clip.  Muting deliberately does not announce -- playing a confirmation at zero
gain is indistinguishable from the feature being broken -- and says so in words.
The label shows the raw value next to the percentage because the driver
quantises to six bits, which is why a read-back does not always match what was
dragged.

History rows expand in place to the transcript, which keeps its line breaks:
each turn is a line, and reflowing them runs the two speakers together.  A
record the model could not judge reads 未能判断 rather than showing a blank cue,
and the reason is shown when there is one -- "画面不完整" tells the wearer to
move, which a bare flag does not.

Then the layout.  Seven cards, a 200px console and a 260px log stacked came to
half again the height of a 900px window, so several cards and their buttons were
below the fold.  Scrolling to find a button means the log you were watching has
left the screen, which for a debug console is the wrong trade.

So the document itself never scrolls: it is a grid pinned to the viewport, and
anything that can grow without bound scrolls inside its own box.  The console
and the log are side by side rather than stacked, which costs one pane's height
and keeps the pairing they exist for -- press a button, read what it did.  Cards
take the height their content needs and the panes take the rest, because space
should go where output accumulates rather than into blank card interior.  The
long explanations are folded into <details>: they are reference material, not
controls, and expanded they were most of the page.

Saving frames to disk moved from the pairing card to the camera card, where the
frames come from.  It was also what made the pairing card tall enough to be
clipped.

The cards' cap is 64vh, which is measured rather than chosen: at 900px the two
rows need 573px for every control to be inside the box, and 58% gave 564px,
which clipped the pairing button by nine pixels.

Verified in Firefox at 1920x1080, 1600x900 and 1440x900: document height equals
viewport height, and all 55 controls are inside both the viewport and every
scrolling ancestor.  That second condition matters -- checking the viewport
alone passed a layout where the cards container clipped a whole card, with the
buttons inside the window and outside the box that was showing them.

Two things the page said that were no longer true are fixed: the pairing card
claimed configuration survives a reboot, which stopped being so when the kvdb
flash backend was reverted, and the volume card said the board "已播报" when the
response only means playback started.

核实到两件事：**日志必须手点"订阅"才有**（没自动订阅），**Wi-Fi 凭据有两条写入路径**（`wifi.connect` 走 TLS、`pair` 走串口）。

下面是建议。先说一个前提，它会改变你的取舍。

# 前提：一半功能是队友的，删它是团队决定

`web_tool` 整个是 424635328 写的，预览/落盘/控制台/日志/配对都是他的。他 README 里写明**落盘留坏帧**这件事是怎么帮他定位硬件 JPEG 码流缺陷的（"每一帧的标记结构都完整合法，只有像素内容能出卖它"）。我删起来很痛快，但那是删掉别人的调试依据。

所以我按**该不该删**分三档，最后一档单独标出"要先问队友"。

# 建议删掉（4 项，都是重复或不划算）

**1. LLM 卡里的「本机 PIN 加密保存」** ← 最该删

5 个控件（PIN 输入 + 加密保存 + 解锁并填入 + 清除 + 两行警告），换来的价值它自己 README 都承认有限：

> 它防的是「有人拿到浏览器后乱猜」。**它不防「整份记录被拷走后离线爆破」**

比赛演示时 key 直接粘一次就行。删掉这 5 个控件，LLM 卡只剩 host/model/key + 写入/读回，清爽一半。（`keystore.mjs` 174 行 + 45 项测试也可以一起退役。）

**2. 「录一段/停止录制」**

跟「开始 + 开始落盘」完全等价 —— 都是连续采集 + 落盘。留一套就够。

**3. Wi-Fi 卡的「连接并保存」**

跟配对卡的「一键配对」重复写 `wifi.ssid`/`wifi.psk`。而且有个绕不过去的逻辑问题：这个按钮走 TLS，**要求板子已经连上**，而板子连上的前提就是 Wi-Fi 已经通了。所以它只在"换网络"时有用，代价是切网时链路必断。

建议 Wi-Fi 卡只留「查看状态」，或整张删掉（状态栏已经有 TCP/TLS 灯）。

**4. 「控制」卡的 6 个快捷按钮**

`free`/`ps`/`ifconfig`/`periph_selftest`/`social_cue`/`agent_camera` 全都只是 `shell.exec` 的快捷方式，控制台原地就能打。留「系统状态」和「重启」两个（它们是结构化命令，不是 shell）。

# 建议保留（演示要用）

| 功能 | 为什么 |
|---|---|
| **会话历史** | 这是产品本身要展示的东西 |
| **播报音量 + 上传语音** | 同上，而且是唯一能让人"听出来"的交互 |
| **LLM 的 host/model/key + 写入/读回** | key 不填 agent 不工作 |
| **一键配对（走串口）** | kvdb 的 flash 后端被上游撤回后，**每次重启都要重配**，这个从"省事"变成了"必需" |
| **预览 + 抓一帧** | 眼镜有摄像头，演示要看见画面 |
| **状态栏的灯** | 判断"是板子没连上"还是"功能坏了"，只靠这个 |

# 建议保留但要先问队友（都是调试价值，不是演示价值）

| 功能 | 队友的理由 |
|---|---|
| **控制台（NSH 透传）** | 板子出问题时唯一的现场手段，串口被占时更是唯一 |
| **日志窗** | 同上；`dropped=N` 是他专门设计成"不可丢"的 |
| **落盘 + 落盘会话** | 定位硬件 JPEG 缺陷靠的就是留下坏帧 |
| **占用/释放串口** | 一键配对要占串口、烧录要串口空闲，这两个按钮是配套的 |

我的判断：**这四项都别删。** 比赛现场出问题时，它们是你唯一的抓手；而它们占的屏幕空间现在已经不是问题了（一屏布局已经装下）。

# 顺手能改的两个小毛病

- **日志默认不订阅**，得手点一下才有输出 —— 新人打开页面会以为板子没日志。建议连上后自动订阅，然后「订阅/取消订阅」两个按钮就能删掉。
- **「读回」和「查看状态」** 这类按钮其实可以在连上时自动跑一次（音量卡我已经这么做了），减少"为什么是空的"。

# 数字对比

按上面删，控件从 **55 个降到约 38 个**，少 4 张卡里的杂项，一屏更宽松，演示路径变成三步：配对 → 填 key → 查历史/调音量。

要我动手吗？我建议分两步：**先删第 1 项**（PIN 那套，最独立、影响最小、收益最大），编译+测试确认没连带破坏，你看一眼效果再决定后面三项。也可以一次全删，但那会同时动到 `keystore.mjs` 和它的 45 项测试，回滚起来麻烦一点。
按你的建议来吧

input.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Open the page like a person would and check the log fills itself.

The subscribe button is gone, so the only thing that can bring log lines in is
the page doing it on connect.  If that is wrong the pane stays empty, which
looks exactly like a board with nothing to say -- so this asserts on lines
arriving, not on a call being made.
"""
import asyncio
import sys

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

URL = "https://127.0.0.1:8443/"


async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        browser = await p.firefox.launch()
        ctx = await browser.new_context(viewport={"width": 1600, "height": 900},
                                        ignore_https_errors=True)
        page = await ctx.new_page()
        await page.goto(URL, wait_until="load")

        # Give the board a moment to be reported as connected, then the page a
        # moment to subscribe and the board to say something.
        await page.wait_for_timeout(9000)

        info = await page.evaluate("""() => {
          const log = document.getElementById('log').textContent;
          return {
            subscribed: log.includes('已订阅'),
            lines: log.split('\\n').filter((l) => l.trim()).length,
            tcp: document.getElementById('tcp-text').textContent,
            vol: document.getElementById('vol-value').textContent,
            clip: document.getElementById('vol-clip').textContent,
            buttons: [...document.querySelectorAll('#logbar button')]
                       .map((b) => b.textContent),
            tail: log.split('\\n').filter((l) => l.trim()).slice(-3),
          };
        }""")

        print("链路:      %s" % info["tcp"])
        print("音量:      %s" % info["vol"])
        print("语音文件:  %s" % info["clip"])
        print("日志按钮:  %s" % info["buttons"])
        print("自动订阅:  %s" % info["subscribed"])
        print("日志行数:  %d" % info["lines"])
        for t in info["tail"]:
            print("   %s" % t)

        await page.screenshot(path="/home/mi/convwork/page-live.png")
        await ctx.close()
        await browser.close()

    ok = info["subscribed"] and info["lines"] >= 2 \
        and "订阅" not in "".join(info["buttons"]) \
        and "—" not in info["vol"]
    print("\n%s" % ("PASS 页面自己订阅了日志，音量也读到了"
                    if ok else "FAIL 见上"))
    return 0 if ok else 1


sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

refactor(web_tool): drop the controls that duplicated something else

Five removals, each because the same job was already being done somewhere
better, and the page is easier to demonstrate with 38 controls than with 55.

The browser key store goes.  It was five controls and a 174-line module to
encrypt an API key under a numeric PIN in localStorage, and its own
documentation is clear about what that buys: it stops someone guessing at the
browser, and it does not stop an offline attack on a copy of the storage,
because the attempt counter sits next to the ciphertext.  For a key that is
typed once per session that is a lot of interface for a narrow guarantee.  The
key field and 写入板子 stay; test_keystore.mjs and its make target go with the
module.

The Wi-Fi card becomes read-only.  Setting credentials from it required the
board to be connected, which requires the Wi-Fi to already work -- so it only
ever helped when switching networks, and it wrote exactly the same two kvdb
keys as 一键配对, which does it over serial and works when the board is not
connected at all.  查看状态 stays, because "is it actually on the network" is
not something the lamps can answer.

录一段/停止录制 goes: it is 开始 followed by 开始落盘, both of which are still
there.

The six shortcut buttons in 控制 go.  Each was shell.exec with a fixed command
line, which the console does with history and somewhere to read the output.
系统状态 and 重启 stay because they are structured commands, not shell.

订阅/取消订阅 goes and the page subscribes as soon as the board is there.  An
unsubscribed log is indistinguishable from a board with nothing to say, which
is the wrong first impression for the pane that exists to explain failures.
The flag resets when the link drops, because the subscription lives in the
board's session.

The cards now flow in columns rather than aligning in rows.  With the shorter
cards a row grid wasted about a third of the window: the cards differ in height
by a factor of three, and in a row grid every card in a row leaves the
difference blank.  Reading order becomes column-major, which is fine for
independent panels.

Kept deliberately, though they are debug rather than demonstration: the
console, the log, frame capture to disk and the serial hold/release buttons.
Frame capture is what located the hardware JPEG entropy defect by keeping the
rejected frames, and the console is the only way in when the network is the
thing that is broken.  Space is no longer the reason to remove them.

Verified with the board attached: 38 controls, all inside the viewport and
inside every scrolling ancestor at 1920x1080, 1600x900 and 1440x900; the log
fills itself (log: 已订阅，补发 2 行) with no subscribe button present; the
volume and the clip status populate on connect.  Host suite 498 checks, 0
failures -- 46 fewer than before, being the key store's own tests.

# 删了什么

| 删除 | 理由 |
|---|---|
| **PIN 加密保存 API key**（5 控件 + 174 行模块 + 45 项测试） | 它自己文档就写明防不住"整份存储被拷走后离线爆破"，因为尝试计数器就在密文旁边。给一个每次会话只填一次的 key 配这么多界面不值 |
| **Wi-Fi 卡的「连接并保存」+ 两个输入框** | 前提矛盾：它走 TLS，要求板子已连上，而板子连上的前提是 Wi-Fi 已经通了。写的又是跟「一键配对」同样那两个 kvdb 键 |
| **「录一段/停止录制」** | 等于「开始」+「开始落盘」，两个都还在 |
| **控制卡的 6 个快捷按钮** | 都是固定命令行的 `shell.exec`，控制台能打、还有历史和输出区 |
| **「订阅/取消订阅」** | 改成连上自动订阅。没订阅的日志和"板子没话说"长得一样，而这个窗格的存在意义就是解释故障 |

净删 **473 行**，控件 **55 → 38 个**。

# 保留的（都是调试价值，不是演示价值）

控制台、日志窗、落盘/落盘会话、占用/释放串口 —— 都留着。落盘是靠留下坏帧定位了硬件 JPEG 熵流缺陷的那套东西；控制台是网络本身出问题时唯一的入口。**屏幕空间已经不是删它们的理由了。**

# 顺带改进了布局密度

卡片变矮之后，等高行的浪费更明显（卡片高度差三倍，行网格里每张卡都留出差值）。改成多列流式，卡片自动填紧，卡片区从 565px 压到约 430px，日志和控制台各多了 130 多像素。


约 20 秒后页面状态栏左上会变成「板子已接入 …（TLS，证书已钉扎）」。

页面上「连接板子」卡里的**一键配对（走串口）**能替你做完这一整套 —— 前提是串口没被别人占（picocom 要先退出）。

# 打开后能做什么

| 卡片 | 操作 |
|---|---|
| 开发板播报音量 | 拖滑块 → 应用，板子用新音量念「音量设置成功」。首次换卡要点一次「上传语音」 |
| 会话历史 | 填日期/关键词 → 查询，点一行看完整对话 |
| LLM 配置 | 填 host/model/key → 写入板子 |
| 预览 | 开始 → 看画面；抓一帧存到电脑 |
| 控制台 | 直接打 NSH 命令，例如 `free`、`ps` |
| 日志 | 自动订阅，不用点 |

不用滚动，所有操作都在一屏内。
